claim: CMC atom schema defines structure for all AIM-OS memory atoms with bitemporal tracking.
HHNI node schema defines structure for hierarchical navigation index nodes.
VIF witness schema defines structure for verifiable intelligence witness envelopes.
SEG graph schema defines structure for semantic evidence graph nodes and edges.
APOE plan schema defines structure for orchestration plans with steps, budgets, and gates.
Data schemas enable validation and ensure data integrity across AIM-OS systems.
CMC atom structure includes identity, content, semantic, hierarchical, quality, temporal, and provenance fields.
SEG graph schema defines 4 node types (Claim, Source, Derivation, Agent) and 5 edge types (supports, contradicts, derives, witnesses, cites).
VIF witness envelope includes model_id, prompt, tools, output, confidence, timestamp, and cryptographic hash for validation.
APOE plan schema includes steps with roles (planner, retriever, reasoner, verifier, builder, critic, operator, witness), actions, budgets, and gates.
CMC atom schema requires UUID format for atom_id, valid modality (text/code/event/tool), vector[1536] embedding, RFC 3339 timestamps, and VIF witness envelope.
HHNI node schema requires UUID format for node_id, level 0-5, vector[1536] embedding, valid tier (S/A/B/C), and authority score 0.0-1.0.
VIF witness schema requires UUID format for witness_id, operation_id, model_id, prompt, tools array, output, confidence 0.0-1.0, timestamp, and SHA-256 hash.
Schema validation ensures data integrity by enforcing strict validation rules for all AIM-OS schemas (CMC atoms, HHNI nodes, VIF witnesses, SEG graphs, APOE plans).
Schema evolution uses semantic versioning (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH) with backward compatibility for minor/patch changes and explicit migration for major changes.
Integration patterns enable creating atoms with witnesses, querying with schema validation, and migrating schemas when versions change.
